Overnight showers and morning lows near 53°F have reinforced subdued heating, while latest point forecasts updated within the past 24 hours show minimal divergence. A 24% chance lingers for 64-65°F if partial afternoon clearing exceeds model runs; higher bins face steep scientific barriers from current synoptic troughing. Hourly KSFO observations will resolve the market by evening.

Updated NiMet daily bulletins and 00Z/12Z model runs later today may shift odds further.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 May '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day by the Forecast for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station once information is finalized, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve to "Yes" until all data for this date has been finalized.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is finalized for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: PAGASA's latest 5-day outlook, issued May 4, forecasts a 35°C high for Port Area in Metro Manila on May 5 under easterly trade winds and partly cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers (30% chance), yet traders imply a 54.5% probability for 36°C as the peak, driven by urban heat island effects that have consistently pushed recent daily highs above 35°C despite similar projections. This aligns with May's climatological average of 34°C during the dry season's peak, amplified by high pressure dominance and low cloud cover allowing solar heating. Model consensus shows limited cooling from minor showers, with final advisories expected later today potentially refining intensity thresholds ahead of measurement at official stations.
